Assignment 03 / Sculpting for Design

Impressions of the Everyday

I explored my memories of the sea through texture, relief, and blue.

Impressions · Plaster relief · Colour

For me, the beach is connected with family visits, college friendships, and moments of reflection. I drew on that relationship with the water to make these marine relief pieces.

01

Returning to the water

During our annual visits to my aunt’s home in Trivandrum, going to the beach was a must. My brother and I would spend hours playing in the water until my mother called us back. Later, the beach in Chennai became part of my college life — somewhere I go to process both good and difficult moments.

I have collected shells from many of my visits. For this project, I drew on the movement of waves, the forms of marine life, and the feeling I get from looking out at the water.

02

Planning an underwater world

I explored a rectangular composition and a circular one in my initial sketches. In both, I planned how to arrange marine forms within a bounded surface and connect them through the surrounding water.

I also thought about the background texture. Rather than leaving it flat, I wanted it to contribute to the feeling of the piece.

03

Making an impression

I pressed fabric over the mould to give the background a textured feel, suggesting waves moving around the other elements. I used different tools to create the parts of the marine scene.

My unpainted relief shows the raised forms, repeated impressions, and winding lines before colour is added. The painted version gives the individual elements a stronger visual identity while keeping the surface texture visible.

04

Blue, green, and the movement between

I used blue to connect the relief into an underwater space, green for the long, curving plant forms, and warmer colours to distinguish other details from the water.

I developed the same marine theme in a circular piece. These views show how the raised elements catch light and cast small shadows beneath the paint.

05

A familiar place, carried into a material

I wanted to capture some of the feeling I get from staring into the waves. I combined a personal subject with a process in which everyday materials leave lasting impressions.

I enjoyed this assignment, and making the pieces led me to plan another beach outing with my friends.
